renderedFields.customfield_11323: The current process is a major annoyance for customers.
renderedFields.customfield_10700: An enhancement request to make it easier for customers to perform a PaperOut on x (20, 50, etc) documents at a time.
renderedFields.description:
Customers are regularly annoyed that they can not perform a PaperOut process on more than x number of documents. We need to find a way to give them a better process for performing batch PaperOuts in Command Center.

An argument can be made that PaperOut diminishes our value, but I think it just gives customers a bad experience with eOriginal when trying to perform actions that are part of their normal business process.

NOTES:

  • Current limitation is due to technical limitation
  • Check with Dev on directory limits to implement this particular feature
  • Check with Dev as to how we're currently storing paper out packages and determine if we should change that process

Things to think about:

  • The Export API returns a zip file in base64 encoded format, we will still need to limit the size of this package to ensure we don’t have timeouts.
  • What is the max file size that we expect a customer to be able to download (50MB, 100MB)?

comments.body:
From a recent customer interview ...
The Paper Out process is a current pain point for Westlake, and volume is only going to increase. Paper Out is required when the loan is paid off. Today, papering out is a manual process performed in Command Center. Westlake needs this process to be automated, and ideally to integrate directly with their third-party mailing service for lower cost of handling. Westlake has an extensive IT team, and would likely build the integration themselves if they had eOriginal’s support.
Kristen meeting with Wyatt Deiaco to discuss.

HuiYing Li

Can you confirm where the paper out package is created during the process? Does it go into the database, or does it get stored on the servers file system?
Kristen Jones , please make sure my initial comment on Westlake is considered. Maybe even you should talk to Westlake directly to understand their use case and pain points.

Internal question:

How does it fail, do we do a check during the request process against our max file size setting?

For Westlake:

How many transactions need to be included?

What documents need to be included (ie entire deal jacket, just the Retail Installment Contract)?

Do they know that they can just include the Retail Installment Contract?
Neal Pettingill is coordinating a call with Westlake to revisit their use case. Will add requirements after we are able to discuss.

We still need requirements and to scope this story out. With timing this isn’t going to make 10.3. Neal Pettingill if we can regroup and get a call set up with Westlake we can start getting movement on this story.
Kristen Jones Re-engaging Westlake, and I’ll push to get a meeting on the books.
1st requirements gathering session scheduled for Monday, Sept 9.
closing. will re-open with a larger initiative
